title: Two companies working together
description: Ledgerly, an accounting firm, is a PAP company to Ada's agent Atlas and a PAP personal agent at Northwind Bank for her. Every approval is an Operation. This is composition: draft 0.1 defines no company-to-company protocol.

parties.name: Ledgerly
parties.role: company to Atlas · personal agent at Northwind

steps.title: Atlas finds Ledgerly
steps.summary: To Atlas, Ledgerly is an ordinary PAP company: Atlas reads its poppy.json and opens a signed-out, pairwise Session. Ledgerly verifies Atlas's keys.

chat.speaker: user
chat.text: Ledgerly keeps my books. Let it pay my Acme invoices from Northwind.

chat.text: I'll connect to Ledgerly first.

steps.title: Ledgerly becomes a personal agent
steps.summary: To pay, Ledgerly needs Ada's Northwind account. It acts as a PAP personal agent with its own client_id and keys: it discovers Northwind, opens its own pairwise Session, and starts Device Sign-In there. Northwind verifies Ledgerly, not Atlas.

steps.title: Northwind proposes; Ledgerly relays
steps.summary: Ledgerly finishes signing in at Northwind and asks Northwind's agent to pay. Northwind proposes payments.transfer. No standing permission covers it, so Ledgerly relays it to Ada as its own operation, quoting Northwind's summary as written.
